verses.1: The one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High, who abides in the shadow of the Almighty, will find refuge.
verses.2: I say to the LORD, “My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”
verses.3: For he will deliver you from the trap of the hunter, from the deadly plague.
verses.4: He will cover you with his feathers; under his wings you will find refuge. His faithfulness is a shield and a buckler.
verses.5: You need not fear the terror of the night, the arrow that flies by day.
verses.6: You need not fear the plague that walks in darkness, the disaster that strikes at midday.
verses.7: A thousand may fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand—but it will not come near you.
verses.8: You will only look with your eyes and see the reward of the wicked.
verses.9: For you, O LORD, are my refuge, the Most High is my dwelling place.
verses.10: No evil shall befall you, no plague come near your tent.
verses.11: For to his angels he will give a command concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
verses.12: On their hands they will bear you up, so that you will never strike your foot against a stone.
verses.13: You will tread upon the lion and the serpent; you will trample the great lion and the dragon.
verses.14: Because he has loved me, I will rescue him; I will protect him, for he knows my name.
verses.15: When he calls to me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble, I will deliver him and honor him.
verses.16: With long life I will satisfy him, and show him my salvation.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "great lion and the dragon" — the Hebrew uses תַּנִּין (tannin), often associated with a mythic sea serpent or dragon; "great lion" is a poetic parallel to the serpent, not a literal animal.
raw:
[1] The one who dwells in the shelter of the Most High, who abides in the shadow of the Almighty, will find refuge.

[2] I say to the LORD, “My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust.”

[3] For he will deliver you from the trap of the hunter, from the deadly plague.

[4] He will cover you with his feathers; under his wings you will find refuge. His faithfulness is a shield and a buckler.

[5] You need not fear the terror of the night, the arrow that flies by day.

[6] You need not fear the plague that walks in darkness, the disaster that strikes at midday.

[7] A thousand may fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand—but it will not come near you.

[8] You will only look with your eyes and see the reward of the wicked.

[9] For you, O LORD, are my refuge, the Most High is my dwelling place.

[10] No evil shall befall you, no plague come near your tent.

[11] For to his angels he will give a command concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.

[12] On their hands they will bear you up, so that you will never strike your foot against a stone.

[13] You will tread upon the lion and the serpent; you will trample the great lion and the dragon.

[14] Because he has loved me, I will rescue him; I will protect him, for he knows my name.

[15] When he calls to me, I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble, I will deliver him and honor him.

[16] With long life I will satisfy him, and show him my salvation.

---
Notes
- v. 13: "great lion and the dragon" — the Hebrew uses תַּנִּין (tannin), often associated with a mythic sea serpent or dragon; "great lion" is a poetic parallel to the serpent, not a literal animal.
